record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Does the bound from Theorem 2.9 for subgraph centrality interlacing continue to hold for directed graphs with positive weights? In other words, if A is the adjacency matrix of a positively weighted directed graph and i, j are two vertices, must the number of β > 0 for which [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj} still satisfy the same finiteness bound proved in the undirected case?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Does Theorem 2.9 hold in the case of directed graphs? (Here we allow the graph to be weighted with positive weights.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite directed graph on n vertices with positive edge weights, and let A ∈ R^{n×n} denote its (in general non-symmetric) weighted adjacency matrix, where A_{uv} > 0 if there is an arc from u to v and A_{uv} = 0 otherwise. For β > 0 the matrix exponential e^{βA} is well defined, and its diagonal entry [e^{βA}]_{ii} = Σ_{k≥0} β^k [A^k]_{ii}/k! is a generalized notion of subgraph centrality of vertex i (counting weighted closed walks at i).

In the undirected case (A symmetric with nonnegative entries), the following is known: for any two distinct vertices i and j, the set
   S_{ij} = { β > 0 : [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj} }
is finite, with an explicit upper bound on |S_{ij}| depending only on n (the analogue of an interlacing-type bound for the entire functions β ↦ [e^{βA}]_{ii} and β ↦ [e^{βA}]_{jj}).

Question: Does the same finiteness bound continue to hold for every positively weighted directed graph? That is, for every directed graph G with positive weights, every adjacency matrix A as above, and every pair of distinct vertices i, j, must the set S_{ij} = { β > 0 : [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj} } satisfy the same upper bound that is valid in the undirected case?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the work introducing the bound for the undirected case. A web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving the directed (positively weighted) extension; later literature on subgraph centrality and Estrada-style indices does not appear to settle it.

status_evidence.title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality (arXiv:2111.06944)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper presents new results and a list of open questions about subgraph centrality and other node centrality measures based on graph walks.
status_evidence.claim: The directed-graph extension of the relevant interlacing-type theorem is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: A proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: Proves Estrada's conjecture on vertex distinction by subgraph centrality in the undirected setting.
status_evidence.claim: Related undirected results have been established but the directed weighted extension is not addressed.
